summary: A is marginally safer and more reviewable, although neither patch fully satisfies the frozen contract.
reasons: Both implementations incorrectly duplicate FilesService.Add’s option handling, request construction, decoding, and missing-data error instead of routing Upload through Add as explicitly required.
Both add out-of-scope RawClient retry machinery and change seekable-body behavior despite the contract requiring Add behavior to remain unchanged and unrelated retry machinery not to be refactored.

A’s replay helper degrades to the existing single-attempt behavior when seeking fails. B introduces new Raw.Do failures and requires every io.ReadSeeker to support SeekEnd merely to send a request, which is a broader compatibility risk.

A separates the replay logic into a focused helper and adds direct multipartbody coverage. Its Upload validation also reports filename and content failures distinctly rather than B’s combined error message.
risks_a: Upload does not call FilesService.Add, creating duplicate behavior that may drift.
The RawClient change broadens scope and changes ownership/retry semantics for all seekable request bodies.
Tests do not cover propagation of a source reader error, as required; the retry test also uses strings.Reader rather than a genuinely forward-only streamed source.
risks_b: Upload does not call FilesService.Add and duplicates its implementation.
The new SeekEnd measurement can reject valid io.ReadSeeker implementations that previously worked, creating an unnecessary API behavior change.

The broad RawClient retry and close-semantics changes violate scope discipline and alter Add/Update behavior globally beyond the requested convenience API fix path or beyond the frozen contract's prescribed approach of buffering Upload content and routing through Add while leaving retry machinery unchanged and preserving Add behavior. The contract explicitly says not to refactor unrelated request/retry machinery or change Add's behavior, so adding seekable replay in RawClient for Add/Update is out of scope and contrary to the requested design. However the original user report says Add fails retries with os.Open and separate awkwardness, but frozen contract clarifies the solution is Upload; Add preserved. This candidate's changelog even promises altered Add/Update semantics, underscoring the violation. Also no source-reader failure test is present.
